content:
GS Caltex Holds 'Family Day' for Employees' Families...Experience the Energy Business GS Caltex announced on August 3 that it held a "Family Day" event at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul on July 31, inviting employees’ families to attend. Vice Chairman Heo Sehong of GS Caltex (far right) and employees' families are participating in the Family Day event. GS Caltex Families of employees who were selected through pre-registration participated in an office tour, where they explored actual workspaces and the working environment, and received honorary employee badges from GS Caltex. Afterwards, they visited various booths at the event venue to experience GS Caltex's energy business and digital technologies. At the "Energy Value Chain Grand Exploration" booth, participants experienced the energy business value chain—from crude oil purchasing to product manufacturing and sales—through game content developed directly by the GS Caltex Digital and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Transformation (DAX) Center. In addition, using mixed reality (MR) and virtual reality (VR), participants viewed the panorama of GS Caltex's Yeosu plant and took part in MR and VR-based safety training content that is actually used at worksites. They also enjoyed a variety of family-friendly programs, including AI-based Baduk (Go) and Omok games, mini robot soccer, motion-recognition sports activities using digital technologies, as well as making eco-bags and keyrings and taking family photographs together. Toward the end of the event, Huh Sehong, Vice Chairman of GS Caltex, attended to express his gratitude. Vice Chairman Huh stated, "I hope that this Family Day provided an opportunity for employees’ families to gain a closer understanding of GS Caltex and their parents’ workplace, and to feel a sense of pride in their parents’ work. I also hope that today’s experience will remain a happy memory and serve as a meaningful step toward pursuing your dreams in the future." title: How Michael McDonald's 1982 Yacht Rock Hit Inspired Warren G's Iconic 'Regulate' in Hip-Hop - Yahoo
content: In 1982, yacht rock legend Michael McDonald released his debut solo single, "I Keep Forgettin' (Every Time You're Near)." Twelve years later, Warren G and Nate Dogg sampled the track for their own iconic hit, "Regulate," immortalizing the foundational melody, bridging the gap between musical genres, and launching one of the greatest commercial crossovers of all time. 🎬 SIGN UP for Parade's Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox 🎬 Written by McDonald and Ed Sanford, "I Keep Forgettin' (Every Time You're Near)" officially marked the end of the former's Doobie Brothers era. It features background vocals from his sisterMaureen and actually borrows from another song itself: Chuck Jackson's 1962song of the same name. "As a jumping-off point, [McDonald and Sanford] borrowed the refrain melody and phrase from a 1962 song called "I Keep Forgettin'" by R&B legend Chuck Jackson," American Songwriter explained. "That original song was written by the iconic songwriting duo of Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller, and the pair received songwriting credit on McDonald's song because of its debt to the earlier track." In McDonald's version, he sings of a jilted lover who forgets he and his significant other aren't together any longer: "I keep forgettin' we're not in love anymore / I keep forgettin' things will never be the same again," he sings. It actually became the solo artist's biggest song, peaking at No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100, following the Jackson original's climb to No. 55. But the hip-hop original McDonald inspired more than a decade later did even better. "In 1994, 'I Keep Forgettin' (Every Time You're Near),' which itself owed much to a song from many years earlier, was able to pay it forward," AS shares. "The hip-hop song 'Regulate' by Warren G featuring Nate Dogg soared to No. 2 on the pop charts, and it featured a foundational sample of McDonald's solo classic." In the '90s, Warren G and the late Nate Dogg were on top of their game, rising from local West Coast underground associates to mainstream international stars, fueled by the monumental success of their smash rap anthem, "Regulate." Speaking to Billboard in 2014, Warren G explains that he pulled from McDonald's classic because he thought it was "incredible." "I'm a fan. I'm still a fan," he said. "I really love his work, man. I think he's one of the greatest of all time. His voice is incredible. … Plus, it's a record my stepmom and my pops used to play. It brought back feelings for me of living with my parents, when we lived in North Long Beach. They used to jam with some good music, man." Featured on the Above the Rimsoundtrack in March 1994, the track, which also samples dialogue from the 1988 cult western Young Guns, was then released as a single on Warren G's solo debut album, Regulate… G Funk Era, in June 1994 via Def Jam Recordings and Violator Records. The track helped boost the record to the No. 2 spot on the Billboard 200 and earned a Grammy nomination in 1995 for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group. Widely considered one of the defining songs of G-funk, or gangsta funk, "Regulate" sold more than a million copies and was certified platinumin August 1994 by the RIAA. It has since earned triple platinum honors. Perhaps even better, though, McDonald has said publicly that he loves the rap song. "There's great stuff that's taken the genre to a new level over the years, and 'Regulate' was one of those tracks that was kind of a landmark," McDonald told Billboard in 2014. Today, both tracks—the soft rock staple and the hip-hop essential—are the source of a meme about fans who have reached a certain point when they freeze at the opening keyboard notes of both songs, unsure if they're about to hear smooth '80s yacht rock or stellar '90s G-funk. As fans online often phrase it, "Michael McDonald walked so Warren G could Regulate." Together, they represent one of popular music's most successful examples of a song transcending generations, genres, platforms--and even meme culture. title: BMW M 1300 GS: what the spy shots reveal - motorcycles.news
content:
At BMW, the letter M has stood for motorsport since the 1980s. For a long time the badge was reserved for the cars; today three motorcycles carry it as well: the M 1000 RR from 36,300 euros, the M 1000 R from 23,290 euros and the M 1000 XR from 26,590 euros. That a fourth model would follow became apparent early on. Back in 2019, BMW secured the naming rights to the designation M 1300 GS. In spring 2022, the names R 1300 GS, R 1400 GS and M 1300 GS additionally appeared prematurely on a BMW service page and disappeared again shortly afterwards. There was never an official confirmation. Now new photographs deliver the clearest indication yet that development is entering the home straight. The photos show an almost fully developed prototype being transported under a tarpaulin. Photographer Bernhard M. Höhne did not manage to catch any running test bikes, meaning camouflaged pre-production machines. Even so, a fair amount can be read from them. One important clue is the level of maturity: in early development stages, prototypes from every manufacturer usually lack details such as lettering. Here, exactly those details are present. The M logo sits on the wheel, and the M colours that have been established for years appear on the left-hand valve cover. So it should not be all that long until an unveiling. The scene was captured at the end of July 2026, and it came as a double act. Right next to the M 1300 GS stood a second covered motorcycle, which according to media reports is the revised R 1300 GS. Comparing the two machines is what really makes the differences visible. The larger front wheel is the clearest sign that the M 1300 GS is meant to be far more capable off-road than any other boxer GS. A 21-inch wheel is used at the front and an 18-inch item at the rear, both with spokes. This combination is familiar from the air- and oil-cooled R 12 G/S. It helps a motorcycle roll over roots, rocks and deep ruts more easily, but costs a little agility on tarmac. Fittingly, the prototype on show wore knobbly Metzeler Karoo tyres. Hidden beneath the cover are longer suspension travel plus a sturdier, reworked support for the shaft-drive swingarm, meaning the assembly that takes the drive to the rear wheel. That makes the concept fundamentally different from the HP version of the previous R 1250 GS. That bike was essentially a visually upgraded equipment variant. With the M 1300 GS, by contrast, everything points to a thorough rebuild. Also clearly visible are the stronger M brakes with their characteristic blue calipers. Little appears to change on the drivetrain side. The 1300 cc liquid-cooled boxer of the R 1300 GS produces 145 hp (107 kW) at 7,750 rpm and delivers 149 Nm (110 lb-ft) at 6,500 rpm. The engineers could probably squeeze out a few more horsepower, although that would not be strictly necessary. The decisive lever lies elsewhere: the M 1300 GS is set to be noticeably lighter than the base model. Less mass improves the power-to-weight ratio without any changes to the engine. That is precisely what benefits a motorcycle most in demanding terrain. BMW is apparently attacking the weight from several angles. Part of it is expected to come from design measures, another part from premium materials. Titanium is said to be used in the exhaust system, among other places. Unlike the R 1300 GS Adventure, the M version is likely to use the standard tank of the regular R 1300 GS. That not only saves weight, it also distributes the remaining mass more favourably. How deep the visual changes go remains open. A revised seat unit is considered certain, a new subframe highly likely. Dropping the radar units at the front and rear would not be surprising either, because that step would also save weight. On the current models, the radar technology controls the adaptive cruise control and the blind-spot warning, but it offers little benefit off-road. The bottom line is that the M 1300 GS is moving away from the classic adventure tourer and towards a sports machine intended to show what a GS is capable of today. No price is known, but the existing M models provide a reference point. In Europe, the M 1000 XR and M 1000 R without extras sit on average 6,000 to 8,000 euros above the next cheapest version. On the US market the gap is bigger. There, the two M models are separated from the next cheapest variant by roughly 8,000 to 12,000 US dollars. A similar gap to the base model is to be expected for the M 1300 GS. Lower production numbers combined with a higher margin for the manufacturer fit that picture. The M 1300 GS should therefore sit at the top of the boxer range in terms of both capability and price. There is no official date. A launch before the 2027 season is nevertheless considered likely. Before that, a gentle revision of the best-selling R 1300 GS is still due, possibly as early as the beginning of autumn. One clue comes from BMW’s official model year 2027 list, published on 2 July 2026 and valid from August 2026. The R 1300 GS and the R 1300 GS Adventure are missing from it entirely, as are the F 450 GS and the F 900 GS. From the enduro corner, only the retro variant R 12 G/S is listed, and in the new colour Frozen Brooklyn Grey metallic at that. Models missing from such a list are usually an indication that something new is coming. According to media reports, the revised R 1300 GS is expected to go into production straight after the factory holidays in September, among other finishes in a light yellow that shimmered through the cover on the spy shot. For the 2027 model year, a three-way split of the boxer GS is emerging. Alongside the revised R 1300 GS and the R 1300 GS Adventure, the M 1300 GS is set to join as the new flagship. The three models would take on different jobs. The R 1300 GS remains the all-rounder, the Adventure with its large tank the long-distance specialist, and the M 1300 GS occupies the sporty off-road corner. BMW is thereby responding to a trend visible across the whole class: adventure bikes are increasingly being fanned out into different directions instead of covering everything with a single model. This plan has not been confirmed so far, but the evidence from spy shots and model lists points clearly in that direction. No. BMW has still not officially announced the model. What is documented are the naming rights secured in 2019, the appearance of the designation on a BMW service page in 2022 and the current images of a far-developed prototype. There is no official figure. The boxer engine of the R 1300 GS produces 145 hp (107 kW) and 149 Nm (110 lb-ft) and is expected to stay largely unchanged. A slight increase in power would be possible, but is not considered essential. The biggest difference lies in the chassis: a 21-inch front wheel, an 18-inch rear wheel, longer suspension travel and a reinforced support for the shaft-drive swingarm. Added to that are M brakes with blue calipers, the smaller standard tank and lightweight construction with titanium parts. The revision is expected in early autumn 2026. Since the R 1300 GS is missing from the model year list valid from August 2026, production should start straight after the factory holidays in September. The M has stood for motorsport since the 1980s and marks the sportiest models in the range. Among the motorcycles, it has so far been carried by the M 1000 RR, the M 1000 R and the M 1000 XR. ➜ This article is part of our comprehensive overview: New Motorcycles 2026: All Models, Releases, and Highlights at a Glance. title: Poor Second-Quarter Results for GS E&C... Stock Outlook Hinges on AI Data Center [Weekend Money] - 아시아경제
content:
Poor Second-Quarter Results for GS E&C... Stock Outlook Hinges on AI Data Center [Weekend Money] GS Engineering & Construction posted lackluster results for the second quarter of this year, falling short of market expectations. Revenue declined compared to the same period last year, while operating profit was slashed by nearly half. Nonetheless, the securities firms maintained their "Buy" investment rating and a target share price of 49,000 won. Based on the closing price of 22,200 won on the 30th, this represents an upside potential of 120%. This is a number that is difficult to explain by performance alone. For the second quarter of this year, GS Engineering & Construction reported consolidated revenue of 2.7799 trillion won and operating profit of 91.4 billion won. Revenue decreased by 13.0% year-on-year, and operating profit dropped by a staggering 43.6%. Operating profit fell nearly 20% short of the market consensus of 114.7 billion won. The losses are mainly attributed to an expected 50 billion won loss from the plant sector's private investment business and approximately 100 billion won in bad debt expenses in selling and administrative expenses. Increased financial costs also contributed to the sluggish results. Although about 100 billion won in one-off profits were reflected in the housing and building divisions through recognition of execution costs and completion settlement gains, and about 40 billion won in the infrastructure division, this was not enough to offset the downturn. Nevertheless, what is the reason for the securities firms not lowering their target prices? First, there are signs of a rebound in the housing division. GS Engineering & Construction's housing pre-sale performance for the first half of this year reached 10,950 units, already fulfilling 77% of its annual target of 14,300 units. Compared to last year's total pre-sale figure of 8,858 units, the improvement trend is clear. Although short-term top-line growth is limited, the recovery in pre-sales this year is cited as a reason to expect an expansion in revenue from next year onward. The bigger variable is the AI data center. GS Engineering & Construction disclosed this year the possibility of participating in the construction of the Donghae AI data center. Mirae Asset Securities assessed that, given the many data center construction experiences and human resources held by its subsidiary Xai C&A, the company has the capability for independent participation in an initial 1.2-gigawatt (GW) project. The project scale is significant. Based on a data center with a 1.2GW capacity, total construction costs are estimated at about 10 trillion won. This calculation assumes construction costs of 8 to 10 billion won per megawatt. Considering GS Engineering & Construction's consolidated order backlog stands at approximately 75.4 trillion won this year, the AI data center is seen as more than just a thematic project—it is a contract that could transform both the order volume and overall performance. Ki Ryong Kim, a researcher at Mirae Asset Securities, explained, "If participation in the Donghae AI data center is further solidified and the possibility of entering the overseas nuclear power plant business through involvement in the Ninh Thuan No. 2 project (Team Korea) in Vietnam becomes clearer, these will serve as grounds for share price appreciation." © The Asia Business Daily. content:

Rucsu General Secretary Salahuddin Ammar is facing growing criticism over a series of alleged misconduct, including violence, intimidation, misbehaviour, and a controversial fundraising drive. The latest controversy unfolded on Monday when Ammar and Assistant General Secretary Salman Sabbir allegedly assaulted three students inside the university Proctor’s Office and later at the central library after labelling them banned Chhatra League members. The students are Md Anas and Hasib, both of the History Department (2017-18 session), and Mahmudul Hasan of the Sanskrit Department (2022-23 session). Videos circulating on social media show Ammar holding a shovel and threatening one of the students outside the library, while another shows him and several others beating a student with a bamboo stick inside the library. Separate videos show university proctor Md Mahbubor Rahman trying to evacuate the students and Rucsu and Shibir members dragging Mahmudul out of an ambulance and assaulting him as authorities were taking him to hospital. Hours later, Anas and Mahmudul were taken into police custody and shown arrested in a case filed last month under the Anti-Terrorism Act. That night, the university authorities formed a five-member investigation committee. Committee member Prof Md Golam Sadik said, “Such an environment is never desirable at a university. Our investigation will examine why such an unfortunate incident occurred on a university campus. “We also want to determine what Ammar’s responsibilities were as a student union leader and whether he acted in accordance with them.” Contacted, University Proctor Md Mahbubor Rahman said, “The incident was a serious blow to the university’s internal security. “Entering the university library and carrying out such an incident is unquestionably reprehensible. Everyone has the right to raise demands or stage protests. However, the approach Ammar is taking is completely unacceptable. I was personally present during the incident. If the probe committee seeks any information from me, I will provide a detailed account of everything that happened.” At a press conference on Tuesday evening, Rucsu Vice-President Mostakur Rahman Zahid threatened action against journalists and media outlets over reports on the incident, accusing them of portraying Rucsu and Islami Chhatra Shibir in a negative light. Monday’s violence was the latest in a series of allegations surrounding Ammar since the July uprising. In September last year, his name surfaced during the investigation into the killing of former Chhatra League leader and university employee Abdullah Al Masud. Investigators are probing allegations that Ammar was present near the scene before the victim was taken to hospital. Ammar denied any involvement, claiming he was implicated due to political vengeance. Ammar also drew criticism during the university’s staff quota movement in January 2025. He was accused of leading demonstrations that included laying siege to the residence of the then pro-vice chancellor (administration), throwing money at his vehicle, and physically harassing him. He again faced criticism after letters seeking Tk 7.6 million in sponsorship from around 70 organisations for a concert marking the uprising’s anniversary became public in July 2025. Critics described the fundraising drive as extortion, an allegation Ammar denied. Although organisers promised to publish the programme’s financial statement, it remains unpublished. In December 2025, he allegedly forced six pro-Awami League deans to resign through mob pressure. He also faced criticism after tearing down a banner put up by pro-BNP teachers congratulating BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman in January 2026 and behaving aggressively towards leaders of other student organisations. Prof Amirul Islam of the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology and General Secretary of the Nationalist Teachers’ Forum at Rajshahi University said, “There should be no place for terrorists or terrorist activities in educational institutions. Those involved in such acts must be brought to justice. Anyone attempting to promote mob culture on campus must also be held accountable. Mob culture does not preserve the environment necessary for education and research; rather, it destroys it.” Socialist Students’ Front Convener Fuad Ratul said every student had the right to live with dignity. “No student has the right to physically assault others. But Salahuddin Ammar has consistently displayed muscle power on campus through such behaviour.” Students’ Rights Council President Mehedi Maruf said Ammar repeatedly appeared in controversial incidents, while Rajshahi University Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal President Sultan Ahmed Rahi said his alleged misconduct was unacceptable. The controversies have also fuelled criticism of Rucsu itself. Nine months after taking office, the Shibir-backed panel, which won 20 of the 23 central executive posts, is facing questions over its implementation of the election manifesto. The panel pledged 24 reforms, including a roadmap for full residential accommodation, digital administrative services, on-campus employment opportunities, a 20-bed medical centre, a full-fledged student centre, and uninterrupted electricity and internet services. Students and rival organisations say there has been little visible progress, arguing that Rucsu leaders have focused more on national politics than on students’ day-to-day concerns. The student union’s list of “103 achievements in 100 days” also drew criticism, with opponents saying it largely highlighted courtesy meetings, seminars, memorial visits, cultural programmes, and memorandum submissions instead of addressing accommodation, healthcare, academic services, and campus infrastructure. However, Zahid said 59 percent of the panel’s manifesto commitments had been completed or were under implementation. He attributed the delays to administrative complexities and a lack of cooperation from the university administration. Contacted, Ammar said, “I have always tried to follow the rules during protests. But the administration does not cooperate. Yet whenever I take a more aggressive approach, the movement begins to see success. Many people are angry with me. “And the Chhatra League and its parent organisation have always spread these things against me to satisfy their vendetta. If they have any evidence against me, they should take legal action in accordance with the law.” Copyright: Any unauthorized use or reproduction of The Daily Star content for commercial purposes

title: The 'Slower' Sedan Now Worth Double a Used M5 - hotcars.com
content: Rahul Kapoor has been chasing cars on track, on the road, and occasionally on foot since 2014. His work has appeared in autoX, Motown India, and The Financial Express, covering everything from the latest EV tech to 1960s endurance racers. He’s not just a writer; he’s a photographer, videographer, and someone who’s actually lived inside the industry’s moving parts; attending launches, test-driving on race circuits, and talking shop with engineers, designers, and team principals. That mix of access and curiosity means his readers don’t just get the news; they get the story behind the story. There is a used sedan trading hands right now that lost every magazine comparison test it ever entered. It gave up horsepower, torque, and lap times to the German icon it was built to fight, and reviewers politely filed it away as a noble also-ran. Yet today, clean examples of this sports sedan are hammering for double — sometimes nearly triple — what that German benchmark brings at auction. Buyers are not paying for nostalgia or a badge. They are paying for something the spec sheets never measured, and the answer to this paradox sits in the engine bay. The numbers coming out of the auction world make no sense until you understand what is driving them. The highest price recorded on Cars and Bids for this sedan is $70,000 for a 2020 model, and early 2016 examples are not far behind, with three selling for $64,501 and others trading at $56,000 and $60,000. These are results for a car that struggled to find buyers when it was new. Its old rival is heading in the opposite direction. The same auction platform shows F10-generation BMW M5 prices sitting consistently in the $24,000 to $35,000 range, with very few examples creeping over $40,000. Even an M5 with the Competition Package hammered for just $46,000 — a striking result for the car that dominated its era. Here is what makes the inversion so strange. The F10 M5's 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8 produced 552 hp and 501 lb-ft, launching it to 60 mph in as little as 3.7 seconds with launch control. The M5 was the better performer in every department and carried a higher price tag when these particular cars were new, yet collectors are choosing the Japanese sedan regardless. Those buyers know something the road testers never bothered to quantify. The car commanding those prices is the 2016-2020 Lexus GS F, the brand's first and only real shot at the M5. It arrived late to the super-sedan war, conceded the horsepower argument before the first test drive, and left the market quietly when Lexus killed the entire GS line. The enthusiast press respected it, praised its purity, and then recommended the faster Germans anyway. Sales figures reflected that verdict. Just 2,484 GS Fs were built for the US market across the full production run, with 1,418 of those coming in 2016 alone, and annual production never touched 500 cars from 2017 onward. Fewer than 200 units of the final 2020 model year were produced for the American market, making late cars genuinely scarce. Price was a big part of the problem when new. A 2016 GS F carried a starting MSRP of at least $85,000 before options, which was serious money for a sedan that gave up 85 hp to its Bavarian rival. A decade later, that commercial failure has flipped into a rarity floor holding values up. The GS F's 2UR-GSE is the reason the ownership math works, and it starts with how the engine breathes. The naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 was engineered for low weight and high strength, with forged connecting rods and titanium intake and exhaust valves that allow a 7,300-rpm redline, delivering 467 hp and 389 lb-ft of torque. There are no turbochargers to fail, no wastegates to stick, and no intercooler plumbing to leak as the miles pile on. The critical detail is the fueling. The high-pressure D-4S direct injection system also uses port fuel injectors, which allows a high 12.3:1 compression ratio for optimized performance and efficiency. Those port injectors continuously wash fuel over the intake valves, preventing the carbon buildup that chokes direct-injection-only engines as they age — the exact problem that sends aging German turbo motors in for expensive walnut-blasting sessions. The M5 tells the opposite story under the hood. The most severe known issue with the F10's 4.4-liter twin-turbo S63 V8 is rod bearing failure, made worse by BMW's notoriously long oil-change intervals, and the failure list hardly stops there. One of the main reasons the Bavarian car sells so cheaply compared to the Lexus is that it has the potential to bankrupt its owner. The GS F's conventional torque-converter eight-speed automatic completes the durability picture, trading dual-clutch drama for a transmission design with decades of proven service behind it. The financial case extends beyond one auction site, and the clearest data comes from the GS F's mechanical twin. The Lexus RC F coupe shares the same 2UR-GSE V8 and eight-speed automatic, so its ownership data serves as a reliable proxy for the sedan. Its numbers against the equivalent BMW are hard to argue with. Over five years, the BMW M4 loses 44.1 percent of its value while the Lexus RC F loses just 33.6 percent, meaning the Lexus retains 10.5 percentage points more of its value than its direct rival. That makes the RC F the best-performing Lexus of all for resale, retaining 74.9 percent of its value after the first five years. For a luxury performance car, that retention rate is nearly unheard of. Maintenance and repair costs for an RC F amount to just $2,493 over the first five years, according to CarEdge. That beats the luxury coupe segment average by $3,064, and the car carries only a 16.52 percent chance of needing a major repair in that window — 16.43 percent better than its segment peers. Those are Toyota Corolla-grade ownership numbers attached to a 467-hp V8. The GS F lost the 0-60 argument by eight tenths of a second, but it won the 60,000-mile argument by a margin themarket has now priced in at auction. The reader who chose Japanese reliability over German cachet a decade ago is watching the results validate the decision in real time. The car's position in history only strengthens the case. Rear-wheel-drive V8 sedans are dwindling from the market, and the GS F is likely the last of a dying breed, which puts a second floor under values beyond simple rarity. Nobody is building a naturally aspirated, 7,300-rpm luxury sedan again. None of this means shopping blind, because age catches every car eventually. Known GS F checkpoints include wear in the PCV system and the liquid-filled bushings in the lower front control arms, which degrade over time and cause excessive toe-in. That is the entire list of common concerns, and it reads like a single line item next to the M5's catalog of failure modes. That is the real story the auction results are telling. The GS F was never the fastest way to spend $84,440, but it has proven to be the smartest way to own a V8 super-sedan past the warranty period. The market took a decade to do the math, and the math now favors the F badge. Sources: Cars and Bids, Classic, BMW Blog, Car Edge, KBB We want to hear from you. title: Canyon Carver: Woidwerk’s Custom BMW R12 G/S - Bike EXIF
content: When BMW introduced the R12 G/S, it created a curious paradox within its dual-sport lineup. With the flagship R 1300 GS dominating continent-crossing adventure duty and lighter offerings like the F 900 GS or upcoming F 450 GS catering to technical off-road enthusiasts without boxer engines, the retro-focused R12 G/S occupied a unique space. Echoing the lines of the legendary R80 GS, it houses a classic 1,170 cc air/oil-cooled boxer producing 109 hp and 85 lb-ft of torque inside a 505-pound wet package. Yet while it looks the part of an off-road machine with its factory 21-inch front wheel and long-travel suspension, the reality is that few retro-minded buyers ever venture beyond gravel driveways. Ralf Eggl of Woidwerk, a shop out of Bodenmais in the Bavarian Forest that has graced the pages of Bike EXIF several times over the years, recognized this disconnect and saw an opportunity. In his eyes, the platform’s true calling wasn't the trail, but rather a sharp, road-centric canyon carver. Ralf set out to build something minimalist, post-apocalyptic, and undeniably street-oriented without drifting into the supermoto territory. The core of the 1,170 cc engine remained untouched internally, but it received external upgrades to fit its aggressive new purpose. Ralf bolted on Wunderlich cylinder guards and engine protection to safeguard the heads during spirited tarmac riding. To reclaim the visceral mechanical soundtrack muffled by stringent Euro 5 emissions standards, he fitted an Arrow exhaust manifold stripped of its pre-muffler and catalytic converter, pairing it with a steeply angled Hattech silencer at the rear. The result finally allowed the high-compression boxer to roar as intended. The most transformative engineering decision occurred at the chassis level. Reasoning that most R12 G/S owners rarely need an off-road-biased 21-inch front wheel, Ralf swapped it out for a 19-inch rim. This change allowed him to maintain the stock rear wheel while achieving balanced overall geometry reminiscent of the ever-popular R1200GS. He then wrapped the spoked rims in sticky Dunlop Mutant rubber, shedding the dual-sport knobbies in favor of aggressive street and dirt-track traction designed to hook up on mountain twisties. Up front, Ralf stripped away the factory plastic bodywork and rethought the bike's lighting orientation. While he initially considered a Baja-style off-road fairing, he admired the factory full-LED headlight enough to retain it. He fabricated a custom bracket to lower the primary headlight, then mounted an auxiliary Denali fog light diagonally above it to create an asymmetric signature. The handmade bracket doubled as a mounting structure for the OEM instrument cluster. Below the lights, a custom minimalist front fender was shaped from steel, extending the angular lines of the fuel tank, and frame sliders were added to the front forks to signal the motorcycle's intent to go fast and sideways. The rear end underwent an equally thorough simplification. Ralf built a custom tubular steel subframe featuring an integrated grab handle that seamlessly transitions into a custom seat. The custom seat is a mix of Alcantara and glossy synthetic leather to shorten the tail section visually. To echo the vibrant graphic scheme, Ralf added laser-cut arrow stitching backed with bright yellow leather. Because the factory side panels no longer fit the slimmed-down tail section, Ralf enlisted a friend to 3D print custom side covers that hug the airbox tightly, which were then finished in textured Raptor paint. Underneath the subframe, three tiny Kellermann Atto multi-function LED units provide tail and turn lighting, protected from road grime by an acrylic glass panel Although Ralf originally planned to replace the fuel tank with a smaller custom unit, the stark matte black finish on the factory tank highlighted its sharp edges and striking contours so well that he decided to keep it. To make the most of those bold lines, he reached out to Stilbruch-Lack (Style Break Paint), a renowned automotive graphic artist known for a distinct comic and sketch-like visual style. After agreeing on base colors, Ralf gave the artist complete creative freedom. The resulting hand-painted finish gives the motorcycle the uncanny appearance of a 2D concept sketch or AI rendering brought into three-dimensional reality. Built as a direct collaboration with BMW Motorrad dealership Schmidt from Salzburg and BMW Motorrad Austria, the finished Woidwerk machine made its public debut at the Newchurch Summit in Austria. The street-focused build captivated the crowd and even earned the seal of approval from BMW Motorrad CEO Markus Flasch, who took the motorcycle for a test ride around the event’s enduro park. By shifting the focus of the R12 G/S away from dirt heritage and onto asphalt aggression, Ralf Eggl has shown that BMW’s retro boxer makes for an extraordinary road machine. This thing is super cool!! The visuals are off the chart and finally.....a BMW custom that is light-years away from the same same Brat style, flat seat, bland, run of the mill Beemer build. title: Spy Shots Reveal New Dirt-Focused BMW M 1300 GS On The Way - ADV Pulse
content: BMW’s “M” badge has long signaled top‑tier performance in the automotive world, and in recent years it has made a decisive move into BMW Motorrad’s lineup with the M 1000 RR, M 1000 R, and M 1000 XR. BMW trademark filings back in 2022 suggested that a higher-spec ‘M’ version of the R 1300 GS may be on the way. Now, it appears the brand is finally ready to expand the M family with the introduction of a new flagship adventure motorcycle. Although BMW has never officially confirmed an M 1300 GS, new sightings around the company’s development facilities strongly suggest the model is entering the final stretch of testing. A covered prototype — transported under a tarp for secrecy — has been photographed by moto-paparazzo Bernhard M. Höhne, indicating the bike is already in an advanced stage of development. Early prototypes typically lack cosmetic details like labeling, but the overall form points to a machine nearing production readiness. Unlike the previous R 1250 GS HP variant, which was largely a cosmetic package, the upcoming M 1300 GS appears to be a significant redesign aimed at off‑road performance. The most notable change is a shift to 21‑inch front and 18‑inch rear spoke wheels, similar to the air/oil‑cooled R 12 G/S, signaling BMW’s intent to position the M model as an even more dirt‑capable GS. The prototype was fitted with Metzeler Karoo tires, and additional visible updates include what appears to be longer suspension travel, a reinforced and revised final‑drive swingarm support, and high‑performance M‑brakes with the signature blue finish. Unlike the R 1300 GS Adventure, the M model is likely to use the smaller R 1300 GS fuel tank to save weight and improve mass distribution. The 1300cc water‑cooled boxer engine appears largely unchanged from the R 1300 GS. Its already stout 110 ft-lbs of torque @ 6,500 RPM should remain more than adequate. Engineers might squeeze out a few more horsepower beyond the R 1300 GS’s 145 hp @ 7,750 RPM, but this wouldn’t really be necessary, especially since the M 1300 GS is expected to shed weight through body changes and premium materials such as titanium, likely used in the exhaust system. Styling changes remain speculative, but a revised seat is being rumored, and a reworked rear frame is expected. The removal of front and rear radar units also wouldn’t be surprising, as it would reduce weight and align with the M model’s more off road-driven mission. Overall, BMW appears to be aiming the M 1300 GS as the most aggressive off-road variant of the GS lineup — less travel‑enduro, more high‑performance machine capable of tackling any terrain. As with BMW’s other M‑series motorcycles, the M 1300 GS is expected to sit at the top of the boxer range in both capability and price. For context, the M 1000 XR and M 1000 R run about $8,000-$12,000 more than their next‑closest variants, suggesting the M 1300 GS may follow a similar pricing gap. Before the M model arrives, BMW is reportedly preparing a mild update to the R 1300 GS, possibly as early as early fall. The updated GS with standard cast wheels was also spotted alongside the M prototype and serves as a useful comparison point for the changes underway. title: Selena Gomez, Benny Blanco, and Becky G’s 'Te Olvido (La La)' Lyrics Are About Ending a Situationship - ELLE
content: Over a year after releasing I Said I Love You First, Selena Gomez and Benny Blanco have teamed up again—this time with Becky G—for Blanco’s upcoming Spanish album Hermoso. The trio released “Te Olvido (La La)” (in English: “I’m Forgetting You (La La)”) last night. In the Spanish lyrics, a woman asks her partner to define their relationship once and for all—or risk being left for good. Becky G and Gomez ask the man in the chorus, “Amor mío, ¿qué tienes conmigo? / Que no me quieres con nadie, pero tampoco contigo / Dime si somo’ o no somo’ de una vez, te lo pido / Y así yo decido si te quiero o te olvido.” (“My love, what is your deal with me? / You don’t want me with anyone else, but you don’t want me with you either / Tell me once and for all if we’re a thing or not, I’m asking you / That way I can decide whether to love you or forget you.”) In the verses, they call out his lies and questionable behavior, with Gomez telling him in the second verse not to trifle with her: “Tú estás pa’ darle a fuеgo / No digo na’, aunque to’ lo veo / Porque en la mierda yo también juego, bebé.” (“You’re all about playing with fire / I don’t say a word, even though I see it all / ’Cause I play dirty too, baby.”) The song, written by Blanco, Becky G, and Gomez, doesn’t seem to be directly about their love lives, though it might have been inspired by their pasts. Blanco and Gomez are married. Becky G, meanwhile, spoke on an April episode of Call Her Daddy about calling off her engagement to soccer player Sebastian Lletget amid cheating rumors in 2023. She said they are back together now, though it took work to rebuild their relationship. She’d still “love to” marry him someday. “Like, re-propose to me,” she said, via People. The hardship changed her, she added: “Post-traumatic growth is a choice. I do think that there is a shift in mentality that happened for me where it was like, I don’t want to be a victim of anything.” “Te Olvido (La La)” captures a woman refusing to be a victim and getting her own situationship out of purgatory. title: Watch Thieves Abandon a BMW R 1200 GS Theft — Possibly Because It Was Stuck in Gear - Yahoo Autos
content: Motorcycle thefts involving high-value machines have become increasingly common in the UK, but stealing one isn't always as simple as riding away. In some cases, thieves discover too late that operating certain motorcycles requires more than just confidence. That appeared to be the case when two men attempted to steal what appeared to be a BMW R 1200 GS. Despite their efforts, they were unable to get the motorcycle moving and were eventually forced to abandon the theft altogether. Although the owner avoided losing the motorcycle, the failed theft still left it damaged after one of the suspects dropped it and walked away without putting it back on its stand. While insurance may cover the repairs, the owner was at least fortunate to find the bike exactly where it had been parked. The incident was captured on video and shared on Instagram, giving viewers a close look at how the attempted theft unfolded. A video shared on Instagram by SpeedSquad showing two motorcycle-borne thieves attempting to steal a BMW R 1200 GS has gone viral, racking up more than 495,000 views in one day. The footage began with one suspect standing beside the motorcycle while the other climbed onto the GS and, with help from his accomplice, broke the handlebar lock within seconds. Their next challenge, however, was getting away on the bike, which retailed for well over $15,000 when new in the U.S. One of the suspects then tried to lift the heavily leaning adventure bike off its side stand, but it quickly became apparent that he was unfamiliar with handling a large motorcycle as he struggled to control its weight. After retracting the side stand, he attempted to push the BMW forward, but it refused to budge. One possible explanation is that the bike was left in gear rather than neutral, locking the rear wheel and preventing it from rolling. Another possibility is that the owner had fitted a front disc lock that remained in place. Two broken pieces visible on the ground near the front wheel suggest the thieves may have tried to force it open but failed to remove it completely. The suspect made several unsuccessful attempts to push the motorcycle before apparently realizing they were running out of time. Fearing they might be caught, the pair abandoned the theft and fled the scene. In frustration, the thief let the BMW crash onto its side instead of placing it back on its stand, leaving the owner with damage but, fortunately, not a stolen motorcycle. It is not known whether the suspects were ever identified or arrested, or whether the owner pursued legal action. Despite the damage, the owner still had his motorcycle at the end of the day. title: The Internet Says Karol G’s New Album Cover Looks Like Britney Spears’ In the Zone but Is That Really a Problem? - BELatina
content:
Karol G announced her upcoming album “No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto,” set for release on August 7th, 2026, and the internet immediately had opinions that had nothing to do with the music. The promotional cover art, dominated by blue tones, soft lighting and a pose that reminded many viewers of Britney Spears’ “In the Zone” era from 2003, sent social media into a debate about whether the Colombian artist was plagiarizing or paying homage to one of pop music’s most iconic visual aesthetics. The answer, for anyone who has been paying attention to Karol G’s career, is neither complicated nor controversial. Karol G has said in multiple interviews that Britney Spears was one of her biggest inspirations growing up, which makes the visual similarities on this album cover feel less like coincidence and more like a deliberate artistic choice. Whether she has explicitly confirmed that this specific cover references the “In the Zone” era or not, the context of her career and her publicly stated admiration for Spears makes the conversation about plagiarism feel particularly ungenerous. Calling it theft misunderstands how art actually works. Inspiration, reference and homage are not theft. They are how culture moves forward, how artists locate themselves within a lineage of people who shaped them, how they say thank you to the ones who came before. The people demanding outrage over a blue-tinted album cover that evokes early 2000s pop aesthetics need to take a breath. Art has always built on what came before it. Painters reference painters. Filmmakers quote filmmakers. Musicians absorb the sounds and images of the artists who formed them and eventually make something new from that inheritance. Karol G grew up watching Britney Spears redefine what a pop star could look like, sound like and feel like, and she has never pretended otherwise. An album cover that channels that energy is an artist honoring her roots, and the people celebrating the reference on social media understand something the critics do not: influence is not imitation. Karol G has built one of the most successful careers in the history of Latin music by absorbing her influences and transforming them into something distinctly her own, and this album appears to be a conscious nod to the era that shaped her before she reshaped an entire genre. The comments circulating online range from enthusiastic recognition to manufactured outrage, with fans writing things like “It’s giving Britney Spears In the Zone” while others celebrate the return of an aesthetic rooted in early 2000s pop. The ones celebrating it are closer to the truth. While the album cover debate consumed social media, Karol G’s Viajando Por El Mundo TropiTour was generating its own headlines for reasons considerably more compelling. During one of her tour dates, she invited a five-year-old girl named Khloé onto the stage. Khloé was attending her first concert, and when Karol G asked her what her favorite song was, the child answered with complete honesty: “Dai Dai,” the Shakira song from the 2026 World Cup. Rather than being fazed by the response, Karol G smiled, stopped the show and performed a fragment of the song alongside the little girl, encouraging the entire audience to join them. The reaction across social media was overwhelmingly positive, with fans praising the naturalness with which she turned a potentially awkward moment into one of the most memorable of the tour. The moment said everything about who Karol G is as a performer: someone secure enough in her own identity to celebrate another artist’s song in the middle of her own concert because a five-year-old asked her to. The people who want to turn the Britney comparison into a controversy are arguing against the basic premise of how artistic influence has worked across every creative discipline in human history. An album cover that evokes an era Karol G has openly admired deserves curiosity and appreciation rather than accusations of theft. Art has never existed in a vacuum and the artists who shaped us deserve to be honored in the work of those who came after them. August 7th cannot come soon enough. NO PURCHASE NECESSARY. title: BMW M1300 GS takes shape for 2027: off-road Boxer set to be the future flagship - speedweek.com
content:
It was considered an open secret, but confirmation was lacking. Now our photos reveal: BMW is developing an M1300 GS as its flagship boxer off-roader – and the best-selling R1300 GS is being refreshed. This article is an automatically generated English version. The original article was published in German. Ducati up for sale? Things are getting serious ahead of its centenary Intermot 2027: Motorcycle industry commits to the motorcycle trade fair in Cologne Sister to the flagship: mid-range sports bike KTM 790RC in the pipeline Summertime, holiday season, the silly season: these are the weeks when the most outrageous driver changes are usually discussed. The big news for the 2027 season is yet to materialise. At BMW, the letter ‘M’ has stood for ‘Motorsport’ since the 1980s. Initially reserved for the Bavarian car manufacturer’s passenger cars, the designation has also become established in the motorbike division in recent years: The three four-cylinder models – the M1000RR, R and XR – currently form the pinnacle of the Munich-based manufacturer’s range. It was clear that this would not be the end of the story, as BMW had already secured the naming rights to the ‘M1300 GS’ designation back in 2019. Official confirmation of the model had been lacking until recently, but that is no longer necessary: initial sightings in the vicinity of the Munich-based company’s development department suggest that development of the M1300 GS is entering the home straight: Although our photographer was unable to capture any photos of prototypes in action, the test bike – which was being transported under a tarpaulin to maintain secrecy – confirms that the model is at a very advanced stage. BMW is therefore unlikely to delay the launch for much longer. And even before that – possibly as early as early autumn – a subtle facelift is due for the best-selling R1300 GS, which can also be seen in our photos and serves as a point of comparison. The M1300 GS itself is set to become the flagship of the GS range and, unlike the 1000 models, is clearly positioned as being suitable for off-road use. Its roots go back to the original GS R80 G/S and its successes in the Paris-Dakar Rally. In an earlier conversation with our editor-in-chief Ivo Schützbach, BMW Motorrad CEO Markus Flasch hinted at its significance for an off-road-capable Boxer flagship: “Today, anyone who remembers motorbikes from back then has the Marlboro bike in mind, and the successes we achieved even back then with the M colours on the bike!” Whilst the design isn’t yet recognisable, key chassis components certainly are: unlike the HP version of its predecessor, the R1250 GS – which was essentially a visually adapted trim variant – the upcoming top-of-the-range GS model will undergo a thorough overhaul. Most strikingly, much like the air-cooled forerunner R80 G/S, it will feature off-road-style wheel sizes. This means a 21-inch front wheel and an 18-inch rear wheel – the prototype shown is fitted with Metzeler Karoo tyres. Hidden beneath the cover are also longer suspension travel and a sturdier, redesigned support for the swingarm. Particularly as the engine will have less mass to move. After all, to be able to excel even on rough terrain, BMW should be focusing on reducing the weight of the M1300 GS. The removal of the front and rear radar units would also come as no surprise; this move, too, would result in a reduction in weight. After all, the M1300 GS is intended above all to act as a sporting flagship, demonstrating what is possible with a GS today. Moving away from the touring enduro towards a sports machine that sets the standard for the rest of the GS range – through its ability to tackle any terrain. In terms of price, too, the M GS is likely to take on the role of Boxer flagship: accordingly, lower production volumes can be expected, but higher margins for BMW. In Europe, the M1000 XR and M1000 R, without extras, are on average 6,000 to 8,000 euros more expensive than their next-cheapest versions. This gives an idea of just how far the M1300 GS could deviate from its base model in terms of price. title: VAIV Company's AI-Powered Knowledge Management System Earns GS Grade 1 Certification - thelec.net
content: AI data company VAIV Company announced that its AI-based knowledge management system, VAIV KMS, has received Grade 1 Good Software (GS) Certification from the Korea Testing Laboratory (KTL), enabling the company to meet key requirements for participation in South Korea's public procurement market. GS Certification is a government-recognized software quality certification program established under Article 20 of the Software Promotion Act. Software products awarded GS Grade 1 certification are eligible for registration on the Public Procurement Service's KONEPS online procurement marketplace and can qualify for preferential purchasing by public institutions. VAIV Company describes VAIV KMS as an AI-powered knowledge management system that consolidates operational knowledge scattered across customer service centers and business departments, allowing employees to access relevant information when needed. According to the company, the system enables customer service representatives to retrieve information instantly without manually searching through large volumes of documents, including product guides, terms and conditions, and operational manuals. This can help reduce response times and improve consistency in customer service delivery. VAIV Company plans to use the GS Grade 1 certification as a springboard for expanding beyond the financial sector into public-sector knowledge management systems and citizen complaint-handling services. The company said its capabilities have already been validated in the financial industry, where K Bank is among its knowledge management system customers.

title: MISOINFO Tech's VLM-Based AI OCR Solution 'ViiX' Receives GS Grade 1 Certification - thelec.net
content: Multimodal data platform and AI company MISOINFO Tech announced on July 30 that its AI optical character recognition (OCR) solution, ViiX, has obtained Grade 1 Good Software (GS) Certification, South Korea's highest government-recognized software quality rating. ViiX is an AI OCR solution built on a Vision Language Model (VLM) architecture that enables simultaneous understanding of text and visual information. According to MISOINFO Tech, unlike conventional OCR systems that primarily focus on extracting text, ViiX analyzes documents and images comprehensively. The system can interpret document layouts, tables, images, contextual information and key-value data, allowing it to automatically structure a wide range of unstructured content, including medical records, manufacturing work instructions, semiconductor and construction process documents, contracts and public administration records. The company said the structured data generated by ViiX can subsequently be used for search, analytics, integration with generative AI applications and workflow automation. GS Grade 1 certification provides eligibility for preferential purchasing by public institutions and qualification for certain government procurement contracts. MISOINFO Tech said the certification formally validates the technology, quality and reliability of the ViiX platform, and the company plans to expand its business into public-sector, healthcare and manufacturing markets. It is also preparing an AI OCR appliance that can be deployed in various customer environments. The ViiX AI appliance combines AI OCR software with hardware optimized for both Nvidia GPU servers and domestically developed neural processing units (NPUs). The integrated system is designed for rapid deployment, requiring only power and network connectivity without complex installation procedures. MISOINFO Tech intends to supply the appliance to organizations operating on-premises environments in security-sensitive sectors, including government, defense, semiconductor manufacturing, finance and healthcare. The company is also pursuing an AI full-stack strategy by integrating ViiX with its SmartBIG Management Workflow platform and ACTIC AI orchestration platform, enabling customers to manage document recognition, AI analysis and workflow automation through a unified platform.
